explanations.3: This tells Docker not to prompt for user input during package installation, which would freeze the build process since no one can answer.
explanations.7: The sed command modifies Ubuntu's package sources to enable the 'universe' and 'multiverse' repositories, which contain extra software like fzf and bat that aren't in the default 'main' repository.
explanations.15: Deleting the apt cache after installation shrinks the final image size, since those downloaded packages are no longer needed once installed.
explanations.22: The printf command with '%s\n' writes each quoted line as a separate line to a file, building up a multi-line shell script piece by piece.
explanations.72: This declares a variable that will hold the name of the 'bat' command—either 'bat' or 'batcat' depending on which one exists on the system.
explanations.83: mktemp creates a temporary file with a unique name (the X's get replaced with random characters) so fzf can write its output without overwriting anything.
explanations.85: The backslash at the end continues the command on the next line; it tells Docker (and the shell) that this isn't the end of the statement yet.
explanations.96: The $(<"$tmpfile") syntax reads the entire contents of the file into the variable; it's a shorthand for cat "$tmpfile".
explanations.104: This sed command strips ANSI color codes (the escape sequences that colorize terminal text) so the script can safely split the output by colons to extract the filename.
explanations.115: The > redirects all the printf output to write the complete script file, replacing anything that was there before.
explanations.120: The >> appends these two lines to the existing .zshrc file, adding the function loader without erasing what's already there.
